readerValues.programmeDescription: Leiden’s Middle Eastern Studies bachelor examines the region’s history, societies, religions, languages and politics. This example follows the broad Modern Middle East Studies route, with basic Arabic language study.
readerValues.comparisonExplanation: No close UCR comparison was found for this documented Middle Eastern Studies curriculum. UCR has relevant regional literature, art and imperial history, alongside comparative social, political and economic study. Its strongest combinations do not sustain the degree’s continuing study of Middle Eastern societies, religions, politics and modern literature. The missing 5 EC and unresolved progression rules remain separate limitations.

curriculum.routeLabel: Modern Middle East Studies with Arabic
curriculum.limitation: The 175 EC shown include 30 EC of approved elective study and count History of Central Asia & Afghanistan once. Leiden’s guide repeats that course in years two and three. The remaining 5 EC and the application of seminar and thesis entry rules to this entrant cohort remain unverified.

componentNotes.curr-5851v2msay: Entry requires a pass in Modern Standard Arabic 1.
componentNotes.curr-5851vmsapy: Entry requires a pass in Modern Standard Arabic 1.
componentNotes.curr-5531vaty: One of two published choices for the second-year elective.
componentNotes.curr-5853vewy: Entry requires completion of year one and 55 EC from year two. The thesis is written within the thesis seminar; the application of the entry rule to this entrant cohort remains under review.
componentNotes.curr-component-26: 30 EC in the first semester of year three for elective study of sufficient level without overlap with required courses. Examination-board approval applies except for recognized 30 EC minors at Leiden, Delft or Erasmus. Programme-specific minor restrictions also apply; Honours College courses cannot fill this space.
componentNotes.curr-5853vclmey: Entry requires completion of the first year. The additional second-year language-course requirement applies to the separate Arabic, Persian, Turkish and Hebrew specializations.
componentNotes.curr-5853vsmosy: Entry requires completion of year one and 55 EC from year two. The application of the published rule to this entrant cohort remains under review.

comparisonScope.label: No close UCR comparison
comparisonScope.assessed: The 26 documented components totaling 175 EC for the Modern Middle East Studies route, including basic Arabic, 30 EC of approved elective study, the thesis seminar and thesis. The judgment considers all known regional historical, social, political-economic, religious and cultural inquiry.
comparisonScope.excluded: The distinct 5 EC replacing the repeated course, a complete 180-EC entrant-cohort pathway, and any unresolved cohort-specific progression or abroad/shadow substitutions. No missing requirement or waiver has been assumed.

finding: Every supported component remains visible once at its actual weight. The negative judgment acknowledges actual regional UCR literature, art and history as well as comparative political/social/economic study. It distinguishes sustained regional inquiry from a missing title/language veto. The missing 5 EC, full pathway and progression remain explicit. Internal trials do not become accepted programmes or display prose.
